newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan refugees move away from Zaire road - U.N..
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees move away from Zaire road - U.N..

text.p: The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said Rwandan refugees at Katale camp north of the Zairean city of Goma moved away from a road on Friday but did not abandon the camp.

Paul Stromberg, a UNHCR spokesman, said UNHCR staff in Goma said in their last radio contact with Katale late on Friday morning they were told that some of its 202,000 refugees were moving away from the road running through the sprawling camp.
"Some are moving away from the main road and that's it. They have not abandoned the camp as far as we know," Stromberg said.
"The Zaireans told us for the past few days there has been fighting between Katale and the now-empty Kahindo camps but we have no information that the Katale residents are caught in the crossfire."
An aid worker earlier on Friday quoted refugee reports as saying the 202,000 residents of Katale had left the camp, about 45 km (28 miles) north of Goma, were on the run and caught in crossfire.
Michelle Quintaglie of the U.N. World Food Programme said radio reports from refugees gave news of the flight from Katale.
